s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to broad-spectrum antibiotics, occurring in the context of recent immunotherapy
salient_findings: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
No clinical improvement with antibiotics or high-dose corticosteroids
key_facts: 82-year-old man with epithelioid pleural mesothelioma
Treated with ipilimumab and nivolumab
Follow-up chest CT showed new bilateral infiltrative shadows after eight courses
Patient reported fever and dyspnea
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative
Serologic testing for various autoantibodies was negative
No history of antigen exposure
Immunotherapy was discontinued
Received lascufloxacin and tazobactam/ceftolozane without improvement
Oxygen requirement increased to 2 L/min and later to 4 L/min
Bronchoscopy showed no airway secretions
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages, and a CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy
Cultures of bronchoscopy specimens were negative

shortlist.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient recently received immunotherapy with ipilimumab and nivolumab, and clinical presentation is consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis

shortlist.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of recent exposure to immunotherapy and presented with respiratory symptoms, although no clear antigen exposure was identified

shortlist.label: Acute interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to broad-spectrum antibiotics, which could be consistent with an interstitial pneumonia

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's clinical presentation and imaging findings could be consistent with cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, although the lack of response to steroids is atypical

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised due to recent immunotherapy, which increases the risk of opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia

raw.rationale: The patient developed new bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT after receiving ipilimumab and nivolumab, and had elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels, consistent with an inflammatory response. The lack of response to antibiotics and the presence of lymphocytosis in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute interstitial pneumonia
rejected.why: Lack of typical histological findings on transbronchial lung biopsy

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and imaging findings not typical for this condition

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR and lack of other supportive evidence
